title: HTTP, JSON, and the developer core capstone — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: Turn the expense tracker into a tested application boundary. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which header expresses a preference for a JSON response?
questions.explanation: Accept communicates supported response media types.

questions.prompt: Why use a JSON parser instead of splitting strings?

options.text: JSON nesting and escaping require proper parsing
Every JSON value is a string

questions.explanation: A parser handles the format’s structure and escape rules.

questions.prompt: What makes a unit test for an HTTP adapter’s caller reliable?

options.text: A deterministic fake at the client boundary
Calling the public internet each run

questions.explanation: A fake supplies controlled success and failure cases.

options.text: To bound waiting on an external dependency

questions.explanation: A timeout limits resource occupation when a dependency stalls.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a blocking operation is interrupted?

options.text: Propagate interruption or restore the interrupt flag when translating

questions.explanation: Interruption is a cancellation signal that callers need to observe.

questions.prompt: Which boundary should validate external DTOs?
questions.explanation: Boundary validation prevents invalid external state from leaking inward.
The request targets an HTTPS endpoint; building does not send it. The request asks for JSON and has a five-second request timeout. The method is GET and the Accept header is application/json.
